messages:
lina (Support): Following up from todays all-hands  a few support-y questions about credits/quota policies people asked for written clarification. Ill drop the main ones here so we can pin an official answer.

matt (Product): Sound good. Short preface: we want policies to be predictable for self-serve users and flexible for customers on contracts.

lina (Support): 1) If a team runs out of self-serve credits mid-run, can they request emergency top-ups from Support to avoid app downtime?

alex (Finance): For self-serve customers we don't proactively top up credits. We can issue one-time emergency credits on a case-by-case basis if theres an active support request and clear business justification. That said, emergency credits are not intended to be a recurring solution.

lina (Support): OK. 2) Are credits tied to an org or to specific API keys/projects? We see folks creating many keys.

jin (Eng): Credits are associated with the billing account (org). API keys are how we meter usage, but credits are consumed from the billing account balance. That means keys under the same org draw from the same pool.

matt (Product): To add  we will make it easy to attach billing buckets to projects in the console soon (expected Q2) so teams can partition budgets within an org.

lina (Support): 3) Whats the policy on unused credits? Any automatic rollover?

alex (Finance): For promotional/self-serve credits: expire after 90 days and do not roll over. For contracted enterprise credits: rollover is negotiable and we document it in the SOW.

rafa (Legal): Also mention that promotional credits are non-transferable and cannot be sold or assigned. Important for compliance.

lina (Support): 4) If a customer hits a quota spike due to a replay or bug, can they get a retroactive refund or credit?

alex (Finance): We evaluate these manually. If we determine the spike was a platform fault or caused by an SLA breach, we may issue retroactive credits. If its an app bug, we generally wont.

matt (Product): Practically, open a support ticket with usage logs and well triage.

lina (Support): 5) Rate limit enforcement nuance  is throttling strict when multiple keys from same org are firing? Any per-org soft-limits?

jin (Eng): Currently enforcement is per-key token bucket. We have soft protection at the org-level to prevent noisy-neighbor effects (automatic throttles if a single org consumes an anomalous percentage of cluster capacity). Those protections are conservative and trigger alerts to SRE.

sam (CEO): Weve intentionally kept default per-key to be predictable for developers. Anyone needing different behavior (e.g., pooled quotas across keys or higher throughput) should look at Dedicated plans.

lina (Support): 6) Billing when fallback occurs (model substitution)  do we charge at the served model rate or request model rate?

alex (Finance): Charged at the model that served the token. We record the original request and fallback in logs so customers can reconcile.

matt (Product): Well add a small example to docs showing how fallback lines up with billing entries and the console usage view.

lina (Support): 7) Anything on abuse/fair-use? Can we revoke credits if abused?

rafa (Legal): Yes. Our TOS includes abuse and fraud clauses. If we detect abuse (automated scraping, malware, mass generation for abuse), we can suspend service and forfeit credits. We follow an escalation playbook: warn, suspend, then terminate for severe cases.

jin (Eng): Tech note: we also have heuristics for synthetic traffic and unusual patterns. Those are fed into suspensions-review queue.

lina (Support): Thanks folks. Last ask: can ops-bot pin a short FAQ link for Support and CS teams?

ops-bot: Pinned knowledgebase draft: https://redwood.company/internal/pricing-credits-quickfaq  draft v0.3. :pushpin:

lina (Support): Perfect. If anyone on leadership wants to tweak wording for public docs, drop edits on that doc before end of week. Otherwise well publish the FAQ as the canonical answer. :thumbsup:
